problem.claim: How to scale sparse autoencoders to recover interpretable language-model features while managing sparsity and reconstruction.

gap.claim: Understanding autoencoder scaling is complicated by the reconstruction–sparsity tradeoff and dead latents.

contributions.claim: Proposes k-sparse autoencoders to directly control sparsity, simplify tuning, and improve the reconstruction–sparsity frontier.
Introduces modifications intended to yield few dead latents at the largest tested scales.
Introduces feature-quality metrics and demonstrates large-scale training, alongside released code, autoencoders, and a visualizer.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that they introduce new feature-quality metrics based on hypothesized-feature recovery, activation-pattern explainability, and sparsity of downstream effects.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report clean scaling laws with respect to autoencoder size and sparsity when using their techniques.
The authors report that all introduced metrics generally improve with autoencoder size.
They report training a 16-million-latent autoencoder on GPT-4 activations for 40 billion tokens.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sparse autoencoders are presented as an unsupervised route to interpretable language-model features, but feature coverage motivates large models.
Scaling analysis is hindered by balancing reconstruction against sparsity and by dead latents.
The authors use k-sparse autoencoders and additional modifications to control sparsity and reduce dead latents.
They report clean scaling laws and generally improving feature-quality metrics as autoencoder size increases.
They demonstrate scale with a 16-million-latent model trained on 40 billion GPT-4-activation tokens and release related artifacts.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs proposed training changes with scaling-law results and separately specifies feature-quality metrics tied to concrete properties such as feature recovery and downstream-effect sparsity.

lessons.interpretation: This links methodological choices to measurable claims while distinguishing scaling behavior from feature quality.
lessons.application: When presenting a scalable representation method, define evaluation metrics by the property they target, then report how those metrics change with the principal scale variables.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the task has no meaningful scale variable or when the proposed metrics lack defensible task-specific interpretations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the functional forms, ranges, or conditions of the reported scaling laws.
It does not detail the modifications reducing dead latents, the metric implementations, baselines, or quantitative comparisons.
The 16-million-latent demonstration does not by itself establish reconstruction quality, feature interpretability, or training efficiency.
